chunks: He narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Zayd al-Shahham who said:

I came to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) with a female slave to offer her to him, so he began bargaining with me while I bargained with him. Then I sold her to him, and he guaranteed the price on my hand. I said, 'May I be your ransom, I only bargained with you to see if bargaining is appropriate or not.' I said, 'I have deducted ten dinars from you.'
He said, 'Far be it that this should be after the guarantee. Did not reach you the saying of the Messenger's father (peace be upon him and his family): "The price after the guarantee is forbidden."'

key_terms.اَلضَّمِنَةُ: Guarantee or fixing of the price

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bargaining after the price has been guaranteed in an Islamic sale?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural integrity of *muṣāwamah* (bargaining) in commercial transactions, establishing that the final price must be fixed before the guarantee (*ḍamīnah*) is given to avoid ambiguity (*gharar*). Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) uses a practical test with the narrator to demonstrate that post-guarantee price adjustments are invalid, citing the Prophet’s saying 'The cheapening after the guarantee is forbidden.' This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency and mutual consent in trade, ensuring that the binding commitment is clear before financial liability is assumed.
